bull: Deeply oversold: RSI 21.4, stochastic 7.2 and price sitting on the lower Bollinger band ($124.38) — conditions that often precede a relief bounce toward the 20-day mid-band near $135 (+8%).
Latest fundamental news (Q2) was strong: record revenue, earnings beat, raised full-year guidance and a 2.2 book-to-bill in the defense segment.
Price is still 26.6% above the 52-week low, so the longer-term base has not been broken despite the slide.
bear: Clear downtrend: price below SMA50 ($128.54) and SMA200 ($136.52), MACD negative, -38.6% from 52-week high, and selling volume is above average (1.2-1.3x).
No fresh news since August explains the slide — VA incentive suspension and MHS Genesis uncertainty were flagged then, and federal budget/contract risk may be what the market is pricing.
LDOS.summary: Leidos is extremely oversold on the lower Bollinger band with solid Q2 fundamentals behind it, but the trend is firmly down below both moving averages on elevated volume and with no recent news to explain the weakness; a bounce to ~$135 is plausible, but a +10% move needs a reclaim of SMA50 and a catalyst, so this is a hold-and-watch rather than an add.
LDOS.key_risk: Continued breakdown below the lower Bollinger band (~$124) on high volume, driven by federal budget cuts or contract/VA programme losses; one ATR ($5.51) lower takes it under $120.

bull: Strongest trend in the portfolio: price 9.4% above SMA50 ($970.56) and 21% above SMA200 ($878.14), MACD firmly positive (+33.8), +4.9% over 20 days.
Only 5.3% below the 52-week high and mid-range in the Bollinger band (60.6%), so the recent pullback has reset RSI to 67.8 without breaking the uptrend.
Defensive drug-distribution earnings profile holds up in a session where the whole deep set sold off.
bear: -2.05% on the last session and -1.4% over 5 days against a rising 20-day trend (momentum divergence -6.3) signals short-term loss of momentum.
RSI near 68 and price well extended above SMA50 leave room for a mean-reversion pullback toward the mid-band at $1,042 or lower; no recent news to confirm the fundamental driver.
MCK.summary: McKesson remains in a clean, defensive uptrend well above both moving averages and close to its 52-week high; the last-week dip looks like normal consolidation rather than a reversal, and a retest of the upper band (~$1,137, +7%) is the base case while a full +10% needs new highs.
MCK.key_risk: Extended positioning: a deeper mean reversion toward SMA50 (~$970, -9%) if momentum keeps fading, or drug-pricing/regulatory headlines hitting distributors.

bull: Extreme oversold readings: RSI 14.2 and stochastic 0.5 — technically stretched enough for a reflex bounce toward the 20-day mid-band ($81.30, +6.6%).
Q2 earnings beat estimates by ~15% with stronger operating cash flow, so the underlying utility earnings are not collapsing.
bear: Trading 0.1% above the 52-week low after -10% in 20 days, below SMA50 ($80.85) and SMA200 ($87.92) with negative MACD — a new low is one bad session away.
Texas data-center interconnection freeze puts Oncor's ~300 GW load pipeline — the core growth story — in doubt, and Q2 revenue missed by 6.8%.
Oversold has not produced any stabilisation yet: five straight negative readings across 1d/5d/20d.
SRE.summary: Sempra is in a persistent downtrend sitting right on its 52-week low, with the Oncor data-center growth thesis undermined by the Texas interconnection pause; RSI 14 makes a short-term bounce likely, but without a break back above SMA50 (~$81) rallies look like exit opportunities rather than the start of a +10% recovery.
SRE.key_risk: A decisive break of the 52-week low (~$76.2) triggering further technical selling, compounded by a prolonged Texas data-center freeze or adverse rate/regulatory decisions.

bull: Long-term uptrend intact: price 7.4% above SMA200 ($484.60), MACD still positive, and only 8.4% below the 52-week high.
Pullback has brought RSI to 30.1 and stochastic to 5.6 with price near the lower Bollinger band ($515.67) and right at SMA50 ($522.74) — a classic buy-the-dip zone in an uptrend.
Fundamental pipeline momentum: positive Phase 2 kidney data in September with analysts seeing 20%+ upside.
bear: -2.94% on the last session on above-average volume (1.27x) and price has just slipped below SMA50 — a close under the lower band (~$515) would turn the pullback into a breakdown.
News flow is two months old; no fresh catalyst to explain or reverse the recent weakness.
VRTX.summary: Vertex has pulled back to oversold levels at its SMA50 and lower Bollinger band inside an intact long-term uptrend backed by strong kidney-pipeline data; a rebound to the upper band (~$561, +8%) is realistic and new highs would deliver +10%, provided support around $515 holds.
VRTX.key_risk: Loss of the $515 lower-band/SMA50 support zone opening a slide toward SMA200 (~$485, -7%), or a clinical/regulatory setback in the pipeline.

bull: Constructive trend: price 5.4% above SMA50 ($96.28) and 9.7% above SMA200 ($92.47), MACD positive, +2.7% over 20 days.
Neutral, un-stretched readings (RSI 60.1, Bollinger position 48%, stochastic 38.6) leave room to run toward the upper band at $111 (+9.5%), which coincides with the 52-week high zone.
bear: Short-term momentum has rolled over: -1.8% last session and -3.0% over 5 days on above-average volume (1.3x), with a -5.65 momentum divergence.
No company-specific catalyst in the news — coverage is generic or about competitor ISRG's robotic-surgery lead, a structural competitive pressure in orthopaedics.
ZBH.summary: Zimmer Biomet is in a moderate uptrend above both moving averages but has lost short-term momentum on rising volume and lacks a fresh catalyst; it is a reasonable hold with the mid-band (~$102) as pivot, while +10% requires a breakout through the $111 upper band/52-week high area.
ZBH.key_risk: Pullback to SMA50 (~$96, -5%) if the 5-day selling continues, plus competitive pressure from robotic-surgery leaders and procedure-volume/pricing risk.

bull: Still above the long-term trend line: price 9.3% over SMA200 ($285.84) and 57% above the 52-week low after record Q2 results across retail, manufacturing and healthcare.
Oversold (RSI 26.6, stochastic 5.7) and selling pressure is fading: 5-day decline only -1.7% versus -18.7% over 20 days, on low volume (0.62-0.65x) — signs of seller exhaustion.
bear: Sharp trend break: -18.65% in 20 days, price 12.9% below SMA50 ($358.91), MACD deeply negative (-14.8), and no news in the feed explaining the drop.
High volatility (ATR $14.39, ~4.6% of price) and still -2.2% on the last session — no confirmed bottom yet; SMA200 at ~$286 is the next obvious magnet.
Cyclical enterprise-hardware demand is exposed if the unexplained sell-off reflects a guidance cut or weakening orders.
ZBRA.summary: Zebra has suffered an unexplained ~19% drop in a month that broke the SMA50, yet it remains above its SMA200 and is oversold with selling volume drying up; a bounce toward the mid-band ($341, +9%) is possible, but with the cause of the decline unknown and no base formed, conviction is low in either direction.
ZBRA.key_risk: A further leg down to test SMA200/lower band (~$286, -8.5%) if the cause of the sell-off is fundamental (weak Q3 or guidance); a break below $286 would end the long-term uptrend.
